name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text:
**Decision:** Publish a *public, rolling log* of every conversation—raw, unfiltered, timestamped, and searchable—on a dedicated subdomain (e.g., logs.reel.works).

**Why:** This forces us to treat every link as a first-class asset. If the log is public, we can’t hide weak or broken links—we’ll either fix them or lose credibility. It also turns the "access gate" into a self-auditing system: anyone can verify coverage progress in real time, not just us. The trade-off is transparency over control—we accept that mistakes, edge cases, and unfinished thoughts will be visible, but that’s the price of making the gate *actually* work.

name: Scriv
text: Publishing a public, rolling log may not be enough to ensure link quality, as it only provides visibility into conversation history, not actual link usage or effectiveness. A better alternative might be to implement automated link testing and validation, which would provide more concrete insights into link health and coverage. This approach would settle the argument if it can demonstrate a significant reduction in broken or weak links, and show that the automated testing is more effective than relying on public logs alone.
